The $25,500 employee deferral limit also applies to 403(b) plans, governmental 457 plans and the federal Thrift Savings Plan (TSP) . An eligible participant age 50 or older can generally add an $8,500 catch-up, for a $34,000 annual total. At ages 60 to 63, the higher catch-up is $11,750 instead. At ModernWallet, we calculated hypothetical cases for the ACA subsidy calculator to show how income and premiums affect the estimate. The default case is hypothetical: two people with $50,000 of yearly modified adjusted gross income (MAGI), a $600 benchmark, and a $550 plan. If every other eligibility condition is met, that case produces a $268.85 monthly credit and a $281.15 monthly premium. Enter your expected 2027 household income in the calculator below. Run it again with a plausible lower estimate and a plausible higher estimate. The results show how a change in income could affect the credit. Use your realistic estimate when applying for coverage, and update your income estimate if your circumstances change. The Kaiser Family Foundation (KFF) 2027 enrollment analysis says accurate income estimates matter especially near the thresholds for premium tax credits and cost-sharing reductions. Locate the 400% federal poverty level (FPL) line. The ordinary premium tax credit range is 100% to 400% of FPL. Above 400% of FPL, there is no federal premium tax credit under the rules KFF describes for 2027. If your income is within the eligible range, your credit may be smaller than it would have been under the enhanced credits that expired at the end of 2025. KFF reports that finalized 2027 benchmark silver premiums rose 13% on average. Compare bronze with silver beyond the monthly premium. Bronze plans have lower premiums and higher deductibles. KFF reports that the average Marketplace deductible rose 37%, from $2,759 in 2025 to $3,786 in 2026, largely as more people selected bronze instead of silver plans with reduced deductibles. Those figures describe 2026 compared with 2025; they are not a forecast of your 2027 deductible. If your income is 100% to 250% of FPL, check the silver plan's cost-sharing reductions (CSRs) before choosing bronze. CSRs can lower deductibles, copayments and coinsurance, but require enrollment in a silver plan. Treat catastrophic coverage as a limited possibility. KFF says that, during open enrollment, catastrophic plans are available only to a narrow group. Eligibility includes people under 30, people whose Marketplace or employer coverage would cost more than 8.5% of their income, and people who qualify for a hardship exemption. Do not count on a catastrophic plan until you know whether you meet one of those conditions. Enroll by your exchange's deadline. HealthCare.gov says to enroll by December 15 for January 1 coverage. Its open enrollment ends January 15; enrollment or plan changes after that generally require a Special Enrollment Period. State-run exchanges can set different dates, so use the deadline shown by the exchange handling your application. A cheaper plan can lower your payment, but it cannot restore a credit you do not qualify for. The credit is based on the benchmark silver premium minus an income-based contribution and cannot exceed the premium of the plan you choose. How ACA Subsidies Are Calculated The federal premium tax credit equals the non-tobacco benchmark Silver premium minus an income-based contribution, and it can never be larger than the premium of the eligible plan you enroll in. The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) describes the credit this way. Revenue Procedure 2026-26 sets the 2027 percentages used for the contribution. The calculator runs five steps: Divide expected 2027 household MAGI by the 2026 federal poverty level (FPL) for your household size. Find that percentage of FPL in the 2027 table below, and interpolate in a straight line inside its band. Multiply MAGI by the applicable percentage, then divide by 12 for the monthly contribution. Subtract the monthly contribution from the monthly benchmark premium. A negative result counts as zero. Cap the result at the monthly premium of the plan you choose. Written as one line, the credit is the smaller of two numbers: your plan premium, or the benchmark minus your contribution (never below zero). Income for the 2027 ACA Subsidy Calculator Enter your household's expected MAGI for 2027, the full year you want coverage. HealthCare.gov states that Marketplace savings are based on expected household income for the coverage year. Last year's income is only a starting point: the HealthCare.gov glossary says to begin with your most recent adjusted gross income (AGI) and adjust it for expected changes. MAGI does not appear as a line on your tax return. Build it in two steps: Start with AGI, which is line 11 of IRS Form 1040 . Add untaxed foreign income, non-taxable Social Security benefits, and tax-exempt interest. Leave out Supplemental Security Income (SSI). For many people, MAGI equals AGI or comes close. Take-home pay alone is the wrong input for this calculator. If your pay stub lists federal taxable wages, use that number. If it does not, HealthCare.gov says to start from gross income and subtract what your employer takes out for child care, health coverage, and retirement plans. Self-employment income goes in after business expenses. Some money stays out of the estimate entirely: child support gifts loan proceeds, such as student loans or home equity loans SSI veterans' disability payments workers' compensation Household size and household income follow tax rules. Your family for the credit is you, your spouse if you file jointly, and everyone you claim as a dependent, including dependents who do not need coverage. Household income adds the MAGI of each family member who is required to file a federal return, so a teenager's summer-job pay counts only if that teen must file. The coverage family is a smaller group. The IRS defines it as the family members enrolled through the Marketplace who cannot get Medicaid , Medicare, or affordable employer coverage. Enter the full tax household size and income, and use a benchmark premium that applies to the coverage family. The Benchmark and Your Chosen Plan The benchmark is the monthly premium for the second-lowest-cost Silver plan that applies to your coverage family, and it sets the size of the credit. Your chosen plan's premium, which the IRS calls the enrollment premium, acts only as a ceiling. The calculator asks for both numbers because they do different jobs in the formula. The IRS settles two edge cases for the benchmark. If only one Silver plan is available where you live, that plan counts as the second-lowest-cost Silver plan. If the two cheapest Silver plans cost the same, that shared premium is the benchmark. Tobacco use changes only one of the two inputs. The benchmark leaves out tobacco surcharges, so enter the non-tobacco price. The enrollment premium is the amount you are charged, so a tobacco user enters the higher plan price. The IRS gives an example of both rules. A $900 non-smoker benchmark is used even though smokers are quoted $1,200 for that plan. A tobacco user charged $650 for the chosen plan uses $650 as the enrollment premium, even though the non-tobacco price is $500. The ceiling comes into play when you pick a cheaper plan. If the benchmark minus your contribution is more than your plan's premium, the credit stops at that premium. The calculator has no ZIP code database and no built-in prices. Its $600 benchmark and $550 plan defaults are hypothetical numbers for the arithmetic. When you apply, the Marketplace estimates your credit from your family size, projected income, and other coverage, and the plan prices it shows are the figures to enter here. A Worked Federal Premium-Credit Calculation In our calculation, a two-person household with $50,000 of expected 2027 MAGI, a $600 benchmark, and a $550 chosen plan gets a $268.85 monthly federal credit and pays $281.15 a month. Both premiums are illustrative and come from no ZIP code quote. The arithmetic assumes every other eligibility condition is met. The credit cannot exceed the $100 plan premium, so the credit is $100 and the net premium is $0. Read together, the two cases show how each input works. Income sets the contribution. When the ACA Subsidy Calculator Does Not Apply The calculator's figure does not apply to anyone eligible for government coverage that counts as qualifying health coverage, anyone with affordable employer coverage, or a household that fails the IRS filing rules. The calculator asks you to confirm these conditions before it shows a credit. Government coverage: a person eligible for Medicaid, the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) , Medicare, or another government program that counts as qualifying health coverage cannot get the credit for that person's Marketplace coverage. Limited-benefit Medicaid that does not count is an exception. Employer offers: an offer for 2027 plan years is generally affordable if the employee's self-only premium share is no more than 10.22% of household income. The test uses the lowest-cost plan that covers at least 60% of expected costs, and family members' offers apply the same percentage to the family premium. Employer enrollment: enrolling in an employer plan, including retiree coverage, blocks the credit even if that plan is unaffordable. Coverage from a former employer, including retiree coverage, can be declined, and the credit may still be available. Filing rules: married couples who file separately generally cannot claim the credit, with an exception for certain victims of domestic abuse or spousal abandonment. A person who can be claimed as a dependent by someone else cannot claim it. A new Medicaid rule starts January 1, 2027. HealthCare.gov says states that cover adults based on income alone may require a monthly work requirement for Medicaid. A person who lost or was denied Medicaid for not meeting that requirement may get Marketplace coverage but will not qualify for savings. Leave eligibility unconfirmed in the calculator to show an explanation instead of a credit. Limited Medicaid works differently. Some programs pay only for family planning, emergency treatment, or tuberculosis services. If your state's program does not count as qualifying health coverage , you may still get the premium tax credit when you meet the income and other rules. The calculator does not evaluate immigration status or state programs. Three facts can reverse an estimate: an affordable employer offer, eligibility for Medicaid or another government program that counts as qualifying coverage, and changes in law or plan prices. It also tells you whether you qualify for savings on a Marketplace plan. Updating Income Before Tax Reconciliation Advance payments of the premium tax credit are an estimate, and your final 2027 credit is figured on your tax return from actual household income and family size. If the advance payments were larger than the final credit, the IRS sets no repayment cap for tax years after 2025. The full difference reduces your refund or raises your balance due, and if the final credit is larger, the difference goes to you. Reporting changes to the Marketplace as soon as they happen lets it adjust your advance payments. The ACA premium tax credit is based on expected household modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) compared with the federal poverty level for your household size, plus the benchmark Silver premium for your coverage family. The income sets your contribution, the benchmark minus that contribution sets the credit, and the premium of the plan you enroll in caps it. How to qualify for ACA subsidy? You must meet every IRS eligibility condition. Income alone cannot establish eligibility. Household income must fall in the allowed range. Married filing separately generally prevents the credit, with a limited abuse or abandonment exception. No one else can claim you as a dependent. The covered person must enroll in a non-catastrophic Marketplace plan and lack affordable employer coverage. Eligibility for qualifying government coverage, such as most Medicaid or Medicare, prevents the credit. Limited-benefit Medicaid that does not count as qualifying coverage is an exception. The covered person must pay the share of premiums the credit does not cover. What is the maximum ACA subsidy? The ACA subsidy can be as large as the full premium of the plan you enroll in, because the IRS caps the credit at enrollment premiums. Below that cap, the size depends on how far the benchmark premium exceeds your income-based contribution. In our lower-income example, two people with $30,000 of MAGI, a $900 benchmark, and a $100 plan get a $100 credit and pay $0, assuming every other eligibility condition is met. What are the ACA subsidy income limits? For 2027 coverage, the ordinary range is 100% to 400% of the 2026 federal poverty level in the 48 contiguous states and DC. That is $15,960 to $63,840 for one person, $21,640 to $86,560 for two, and $33,000 to $132,000 for four. Alaska and Hawaii use higher poverty guidelines, and income inside the range does not establish eligibility on its own. Is ACA subsidy based on adjusted gross income? The ACA subsidy is based on modified adjusted gross income, which starts with adjusted gross income from line 11 of Form 1040. You add untaxed foreign income, non-taxable Social Security benefits, and tax-exempt interest, and you leave out Supplemental Security Income. For many people the two figures are the same or very close. Sources We prioritize primary sources for rules, formulas, rates, limits, and definitions. At ModernWallet, we base that advice on Google's published descriptions of what Gemini can access and what happens when you link an account. Google says Gemini can read linked account information but cannot move or invest your money. That limit concerns what Gemini can do. It does not limit the account data stored while the connection is active. Google Wallet uses Plaid to link financial accounts. The published pages considered here do not answer how long Gemini keeps chat content containing account details or how Plaid treats data after you unlink an account inside Google Wallet. Tools for this journey Monthly Budget Calculator → Should You Connect Your Bank Accounts to Gemini? Connect your bank accounts to Gemini through Google Wallet if you want to ask questions about spending and accept the account-data and chat-activity trade-offs. Google says Gemini can use transactions from linked accounts to review expenses and suggest budgets. Google also says its access is read-only: Gemini cannot move, manage or invest your money. You can start with Google Wallet information without linking a bank account through Plaid. The Gemini Apps Help page describes Wallet questions about available rewards, special offers, boarding passes and airline loyalty numbers. Linking a financial account through Plaid adds transaction and balance information for spending questions. Decide whether those added answers are worth sharing your account information before linking. Do not connect if you want transaction history kept out of Gemini. A manual budget lets you work from amounts you enter yourself. The connection is also unavailable to people using work, school or supervised Google Accounts, and to people under 18 or outside the United States. Google says the Wallet feature requires Keep Activity to be on. If saved Gemini chats are unacceptable to you, that requirement settles the decision. Google lets you turn the Wallet connection off later. Removing information already used in a chat takes another action: you must delete the chats containing it. Unlinking a financial account inside Wallet is separate again. Those are distinct decisions about Gemini access, chat history and the bank link, so consider all three before opting in. What Gemini Can See Through Google Wallet and Plaid Gemini can use Google Wallet information and transaction data from financial accounts you link through services such as Plaid. Google's Connected Apps Help page lists payment methods, receipts, data from Google services saved in Wallet and linked financial account information. The Wallet-specific Help page says Gemini can summarize expenses, offer budgeting tips, and check rewards or special offers associated with cards and passes. Google's examples show the kinds of questions the connection is meant to answer. You can ask how much you spent on groceries last month. You can ask about subscriptions across linked accounts and whether recurring charges rose in price this year. Another example asks Gemini to review last year's gifts and travel transactions and suggest a holiday budget. Google's launch post also describes a spending review aimed at saving $1,000 over the next three months. It says Gemini can generate charts for cash flow, asset allocation and budgets in the chat. Those are examples of prompts and described responses, not a promise that a suggested budget will save $1,000. Google says you connect Wallet under Connected Apps in Gemini's Personal Intelligence settings. You can then tag @Google Wallet in a prompt. If Gemini does not use Wallet when you expect it to, Google's Help page says to mention Google Wallet or add @Google Wallet to the question. A bank link is not the only type of financial link described in the launch material. Plaid's announcement says people can link bank accounts, credit cards, loans and investment accounts to Google Wallet through Plaid. The useful question before linking any of them is whether you want Gemini to draw on the resulting financial information for answers in chat. What Gemini Cannot Do With Your Money Google says the Google Wallet connection gives Gemini read-only access to linked accounts, so Gemini cannot move, manage or invest your money. Google's Help page also says Gemini cannot make transactions with Wallet payment methods or update or delete connected financial accounts. You make account changes in Google Wallet settings. Judge the connection's privacy cost separately from its inability to make a payment. What Google and Plaid Store While Your Accounts Are Linked Google Pay Help says both Google and Plaid store financial and identity information while an account is linked through Plaid. Its list includes a credit card or bank account number, a bank routing number when applicable, transaction history, account balance, name, address, phone number and email address. Google says Plaid collects and uses your financial institution login information to access your account and obtain transaction and balance information. Plaid says it does not share your financial institution username and password with apps. Plaid also says it transfers data through its application programming interface (API) and uses Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) 256-bit and Transport Layer Security (TLS) encryption. Those statements describe Plaid's handling of a connection. They do not remove the account numbers, balances, transactions and identity details that Google's Help page says both organizations store while an account is linked. The Gemini setting adds a separate record to consider. Google's Wallet Help page says Keep Activity must be on to connect Google Wallet. While Keep Activity is on, Gemini chats are saved in Gemini Apps Activity. A spending question can therefore become part of a saved chat as well as an answer drawn from linked information. You can review what you plan to link before turning on the Gemini connection. If you need a grocery total, consider whether sharing the listed account and identity information is an acceptable way to get it. Who Can Use It Today Google says Google Wallet in Gemini is available to eligible adults in the United States using a personal Google Account. You must be at least 18, use English and have Keep Activity on. The feature works in the Gemini mobile app and the Gemini web app at gemini.google.com. Google's Help page says it is unavailable with work, school or supervised Google Accounts, and does not work in certain Gemini features, including Gems and Gemini Live. Google's November 13, 2026, launch post describes a rollout to all Gemini app users in the United States across the web and mobile apps on Android and iOS. Its Help page says Google is making the feature available gradually, so an eligible person may not see it yet. If Connected Apps does not show Google Wallet, gradual availability is one possibility. Keep Activity being off or signing in with an ineligible account would also prevent the connection under Google's stated requirements. Availability is separate from whether a particular bank link remains connected. Google Pay Help says a bank can interrupt a link for security maintenance, credentials can change, a linked card can expire, or an account may no longer be found. It also lists unsupported multi-factor authentication (MFA) as a possible cause. For an account that was linked and then disconnected, Google directs you to Settings, Accounts linked with Plaid, then Reconnect. Google says transactions can take several minutes to appear after linking or reconnecting. How to Turn Off Google Wallet in Gemini and Delete Your Data Removing linked financial information from Gemini requires you to address both the Wallet connection and chats containing that information. Google's Gemini Help page says disconnecting the app alone can leave information in a past chat. Deleting chats alone can leave Gemini able to find information through the connected app. Unlinking the underlying account in Google Wallet is a further, separate step. Disconnect Google Wallet in Gemini. In the mobile app, open Menu, tap your profile picture or initial, then choose Personal Intelligence and Connected Apps. Turn Google Wallet off. On the Gemini web app, open Menu, Settings, Personal Intelligence and Connected Apps, then use More options and Disconnect. Delete chats containing the information. Use Gemini Apps Activity or Recent chats to delete all chats that contain the account information you want removed. Google says you must both delete those chats and disconnect the app. If you skip either action, Gemini might still use information from the remaining chat or connected app. Unlink financial accounts if you also want to end the bank connection. On the Google Wallet website, choose Settings, then Accounts linked with Plaid. Select an account, click Unlink and confirm. Google Pay Help says Google deletes the transaction history associated with an account when you remove that account from Google Wallet. Manage data held by Plaid separately. Plaid says its Portal lets you disconnect accounts from apps or delete your data from Plaid's systems. Google Pay Help says Plaid continues to store data for accounts linked through Plaid with a non-Google service. Manage those connections through Plaid. The pages considered here do not say how Plaid treats data after you unlink an account inside Google Wallet, so do not treat a Wallet unlink as a stated Plaid deletion step. Google's launch post also says you can open Profile, Personal Intelligence and Memory Summary to view, refine or remove details Gemini saved about your preferences, interests and goals. Memory Summary controls are distinct from deleting chats containing financial information. Turning Personal Intelligence off for one chat does not stop that chat from being saved to Gemini Apps Activity or used to personalize another response. Google says to use a temporary chat if you want to chat without saving activity to your Google Account. Privacy Trade-Offs for Budgeting The privacy trade-off is whether conversational answers about spending are worth linking financial information to Google Wallet and Gemini. Google's examples include reviewing last quarter's spending, finding recurring subscriptions and using last year's gifts and travel spending to suggest a holiday budget. A question about rewards or a boarding pass may use Wallet information without the additional step of linking a financial account through Plaid. For questions about transactions across linked accounts, the Plaid link supplies the account information Gemini uses. In our reading of Google's Help pages, read-only access settles one concern: Gemini cannot use the connected app to move money or make a Wallet payment. Google Pay Help says Google and Plaid store account details, balances, transaction history and basic identity information while accounts are linked. Google's Gemini Help page requires Keep Activity on for the connection, which means chats are saved in Gemini Apps Activity. Three further points come from the published material used for this decision: The pages do not answer how long Gemini keeps chat content that contains account details. They do not answer how Plaid treats your data after you unlink an account inside Google Wallet. Google's statement that it deletes that account's transaction history is a statement about Google's handling, not Plaid's. Google's Connected Apps data page says human reviewers review a subset of data processed by Gemini, including summaries, excerpts and inferences from Google Wallet and payment services information. It also says Gemini Apps activity can be used to improve Google services, including training generative AI models, when Keep Activity is on. If those gaps affect your choice, leave the bank link off. You can enter figures yourself in the monthly budget calculator rather than connecting an account to Gemini. If you want to compare other approaches to tracking spending, the best budgeting apps list covers alternatives. Decide how much account access you are willing to grant before choosing one. For an adult in the United States using a personal Google Account, connecting makes sense only if the spending questions are useful enough to justify the listed storage and saved chats. Skip the connection if you want transactions kept out of an AI product. Work, school and supervised accounts are ineligible. A published answer on Gemini chat retention or Plaid's handling after a Wallet unlink could change the privacy assessment. So could a change to Google's stated read-only access or data-use terms. Check Google Wallet in Gemini's requirements on Google's Wallet Help page before you opt in. Frequently asked questions Is Google Wallet in Gemini safe? Google says Gemini's access is read-only, so it cannot move, manage or invest money through the connection. That is not a safety guarantee. Google Pay Help says Google and Plaid store account details and transaction history while an account is linked. Google says human reviewers review a subset of Connected Apps data, including Wallet inferences. The pages considered here do not say how long Gemini keeps chat content containing account details. Is Google Wallet in Gemini free? The Google pages considered here do not state a price for the Wallet connection. Plaid says it does not charge you to connect accounts and that the app pays Plaid a fee. Its consumer page names Venmo and Oportun as examples, not Google Wallet. That does not establish a price for every account or service you might use. How do I turn off Google Wallet in Gemini? Turn off Google Wallet under Personal Intelligence and Connected Apps in Gemini. To remove information Gemini may still use from past conversations, also delete every chat containing it from Gemini Apps Activity or Recent chats. Google says both actions are needed. If you also want to remove a linked financial account, unlink it separately under Accounts linked with Plaid in Google Wallet settings. Can Gemini move money or pay bills from Google Wallet? No. Google says the connected app gives Gemini read-only access and cannot move, manage or invest money. Google's Help page also says Gemini cannot make transactions using Wallet payment methods. Does Google Wallet in Gemini work with a work account? No. Google says the connection requires a personal Google Account and is unavailable for work, school and supervised accounts. You must also be at least 18, be in the United States, use English and have Keep Activity on. Why is Google Wallet in Gemini not working for me? Google says the feature is becoming available gradually, even though its launch post describes a rollout across the United States. Check the eligibility requirements on Google's Wallet Help page , including account type, age, location, language and Keep Activity. If an account was previously linked but disconnected, Google Pay Help gives reconnect steps under Settings and Accounts linked with Plaid. mainEntity.name: Is Google Wallet in Gemini safe?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google says Gemini's access is read-only, so it cannot move, manage or invest money through the connection. That is not a safety guarantee. Google Pay Help says Google and Plaid store account details and transaction history while an account is linked. Google says human reviewers review a subset of Connected Apps data, including Wallet inferences. The pages considered here do not say how long Gemini keeps chat content containing account details.

mainEntity.name: Is Google Wallet in Gemini free?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Google pages considered here do not state a price for the Wallet connection. Plaid says it does not charge you to connect accounts and that the app pays Plaid a fee. Its consumer page names Venmo and Oportun as examples, not Google Wallet. That does not establish a price for every account or service you might use.

mainEntity.name: How do I turn off Google Wallet in Gemini?

acceptedAnswer.text: Turn off Google Wallet under Personal Intelligence and Connected Apps in Gemini. To remove information Gemini may still use from past conversations, also delete every chat containing it from Gemini Apps Activity or Recent chats. Google says both actions are needed. If you also want to remove a linked financial account, unlink it separately under Accounts linked with Plaid in Google Wallet settings.

mainEntity.name: Can Gemini move money or pay bills from Google Wallet?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Google says the connected app gives Gemini read-only access and cannot move, manage or invest money. Google's Help page also says Gemini cannot make transactions using Wallet payment methods.

mainEntity.name: Does Google Wallet in Gemini work with a work account?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Google says the connection requires a personal Google Account and is unavailable for work, school and supervised accounts. You must also be at least 18, be in the United States, use English and have Keep Activity on.

mainEntity.name: Why is Google Wallet in Gemini not working for me?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google says the feature is becoming available gradually, even though its launch post describes a rollout across the United States. Check the eligibility requirements on Google's Wallet Help page, including account type, age, location, language and Keep Activity. If an account was previously linked but disconnected, Google Pay Help gives reconnect steps under Settings and Accounts linked with Plaid.

We ranked seven apps across free and paid tiers, manual-entry and bank-synced options, and different budgeting methods, so you can find the tool that matches how you actually think about money. We compared each app on setup time, how clearly it shows what's left to spend, bank-sync reliability, bill and subscription tracking, and whether the free tier is genuinely usable or merely a preview of the paid version. We also weighed whether a genuinely useful free tier exists, since many budgeting apps only became useful after a paywall in recent years. #1 YNAB (You Need a Budget) Best for: People who want the most effective budgeting method and are willing to learn it YNAB uses zero-based budgeting — every dollar you have gets assigned a job the moment it arrives, so nothing sits unaccounted for. It links to your bank, categorizes spending, and shows in real time what's left in each category. The method takes a few weeks to click, but users who stick with it consistently report the biggest behavior change of any app on this list — mainly because it forces a spending decision up front instead of after the fact. It's less prescriptive than YNAB — you set category targets and Monarch tracks progress against them rather than forcing a zero-based allocation. Its net worth and cash flow views are some of the cleanest available, which makes it a good fit for people who want budgeting and long-term financial tracking in one place instead of two apps. Strengths Combines budgeting with net worth and investment tracking Custom categories and rules apply automatically to future transactions Clean, fast interface with shared-household support Recurring bill detection separate from one-off spending Limitations $14.99/month or $99.99/year — no permanently free tier Less rigorous than YNAB if your goal is to change spending habits, not just track them Investment tracking is lighter than a dedicated portfolio tool Pricing: $14.99/month or $99.99/year. 7-day free trial. #3 Rocket Money Best for: People whose biggest budget leak is forgotten subscriptions and recurring bills Rocket Money's core feature is finding every recurring charge on your linked accounts — streaming services, memberships, subscriptions you forgot about — and letting you cancel them from inside the app. Its free tier covers bill tracking, spending breakdowns, and a basic budget. The paid Premium tier adds bill negotiation (Rocket Money calls providers on your behalf to lower bills like internet or phone) and a "Smart Savings" auto-transfer feature, priced on a pay-what-you-choose model. It's a strong pick if you want an app that feels effortless to check daily, though the platform restriction rules it out for Android or Windows households. For most people who want the biggest behavior change, YNAB is worth the $109/year — zero-based budgeting is the most consistently effective method for actually spending less. If you want less discipline and more of a dashboard, Monarch Money gives you budgeting, net worth, and investments in one place. If your main problem is forgotten subscriptions and creeping recurring bills, start with Rocket Money's free tier before paying for anything else. PocketGuard is the fastest to set up if you just want a single safe-to-spend number without building categories. If you'd rather not link your bank account at all, Goodbudget's envelope system and EveryDollar's free manual tier both work entirely offline of your bank. Copilot is the pick if you're an Apple household that cares about design above all else. Run your numbers first with our household budget calculator — knowing your actual income and expense split makes any of these apps more useful from day one. Are budgeting apps safe to use? Reputable budgeting apps use bank-level, read-only connections through licensed data aggregators like Plaid or MX — the app can see your balances and transactions but cannot move money or make changes to your accounts. None of the apps on this list can withdraw funds or initiate payments on your behalf. The real risk with any linked app is the same as with online banking generally: use a unique password and enable two-factor authentication on both your bank and the budgeting app. If you're not comfortable linking accounts at all, Goodbudget and EveryDollar's free tier work entirely on manual entry with no bank connection required. Which budgeting method should you use? Zero-based budgeting — assigning every dollar a job before you spend it — is the method most consistently linked to real spending change, which is why YNAB and EveryDollar both use it. It takes more setup time but gives the clearest picture of where money goes. Envelope budgeting (Goodbudget) is a simpler, more visual version of the same idea, organized around category limits rather than assigning every single dollar. It's a good middle ground if zero-based budgeting feels like too much maintenance. If you don't want to budget at a granular level at all, a simple 50/30/20 split (50% needs, 30% wants, 20% savings) tracked in Monarch Money or PocketGuard gives you guardrails without daily category management. Our 50/30/20 budget calculator can show you those numbers in under a minute. Do you need a bank-linked app, or is manual entry enough? Bank-linked apps (YNAB, Monarch, Rocket Money, PocketGuard, Copilot) save time because transactions import automatically, but they require you to trust the app with read access to your accounts. Manual-entry apps (Goodbudget, and EveryDollar's free tier) take more discipline to keep updated but avoid linking financial credentials entirely. If you tend to abandon habits that require daily upkeep, a bank-linked app is the more realistic long-term choice — the data shows up whether or not you remembered to log in. If you specifically want to avoid linking accounts, budget the extra 5–10 minutes a week that manual entry requires. Frequently asked questions What is the best free budgeting app? Protect the account further with a unique password and two-factor authentication. If you'd rather not link a bank account at all, Goodbudget and EveryDollar's free tier work on manual entry only. What is the best budgeting app that doesn't require linking a bank account? Goodbudget is built entirely around manual entry and envelope budgeting — it never requires a bank connection on any tier. EveryDollar's free tier also works without bank sync, though its paid Plus tier adds optional bank linking. What is the best budgeting app for beginners? PocketGuard is the fastest to start with because its core "In My Pocket" feature gives you a single safe-to-spend number without building detailed categories first. For beginners who want to build a real budgeting habit rather than just check a number, Monarch Money's category-target approach is more forgiving than YNAB's stricter zero-based method while still teaching good habits.
